records.name: Women in the Life Association
records.notes: IRS-only lead. The website field on the tax form is a name, not a web address, so there was no site to fetch. One search for the exact name found no matching group (results were Women In Bio, a national network, and Women In Transition, a different group), so no public presence was found. The filed address is an apartment unit and the contact is a person, so this looks like a private filer with no public way in. Not verified as a public group.

records.name: Y-Math
records.notes: IRS lists this as Y-Math Inc, a small nonprofit filer (990-N). The website (2 pages read) is a tutoring service: a free math assessment, then a learning plan for students in grades 3 to 8, plus a donate link. No public sessions, groups, volunteer roles or pricing were found. Treated as a tutoring service a family enrolls in, not a joinable community group, so not_a_group. No dated news or events; status is probably_active because the site works but shows no dates. The only date on the site is a copyright footer, so no last_sign_of_life is recorded.

notes: Batch had two IRS-sourced groups. Women in the Life Association: website field is a name, not a URL, so one search was used and nothing public was found; hidden as private. Y-Math Inc: a tutoring service with a working site, not a community group; recorded as not_a_group. The second search was not needed. No blocks, no rate limiting, no leads from either site. Budget not exhausted: 1 of 2 searches, 2 fetches.
